summary: Build supply chain risk mapping and scenario planning skills with ISO 31000, SCOR, dashboards, and practical mitigation exercises. Enroll today.
lede: Supply chain risk mapping and scenario planning help professionals identify network vulnerabilities and test responses to disruption. Designed for people working in supply chain, procurement, logistics, operations, continuity, or risk, the course covers mapping supplier dependencies, prioritizing exposure, and developing realistic disruption scenarios. Learners also create mitigation plans and monitoring dashboards to support decisions about suppliers, transport, inventory, and escalation.
audienceIntro: This course is for professionals who already work inside supply chain, procurement, logistics, operations, continuity, or risk functions and need a practical way to map exposure and plan for disruption. It is suited to you if you are responsible for decisions that affect suppliers, service levels, inventory, or escalation reporting, and you need tools that translate uncertainty into action. Supply Chain Analysts who map dependency risk and service exposure. Procurement Managers who evaluate supplier concentration and mitigation options. Logistics Coordinators who monitor lane disruption and contingency triggers. Operations Managers who balance continuity, inventory, and service targets. Supply Chain Risk Analysts who score exposure and maintain risk registers. Business Continuity Specialists who align response plans with disruption scenarios. Inventory Planners who test safety stock and buffering assumptions. Supplier Development Managers who track recovery capacity and resilience gaps. Operations Directors who report disruption readiness to senior leadership. Compliance and Governance Officers who review supplier and continuity controls.
prerequisites: You should come prepared with familiarity in supply chain processes, basic supplier and inventory terminology, and comfort working with spreadsheet-based analysis. A laptop is required for mapping, scoring, and dashboard exercises, and any internal supply chain data you can share safely will improve the realism of the applied work.
